questions.title: Which DRC province will WHO identify as experiencing a surge in weekly Ebola cases in mid-September 2026?
questions.background: The Democratic Republic of Congo declared an Ebola outbreak in May 2026.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : WHO public statements about the DRC Ebola outbreak, including statements quoted in contemporaneous reputable news reporting. Resolution Window : Resolve to the province explicitly identified by WHO as experiencing surging weekly Ebola cases in its outbreak assessment publicly reported between September 10 and September 16, 2026. Accepted Answer Format : The name of the province.
questions.current_reasoning: WHO's June 19, 2026 Disease Outbreak News (DON608) reports 896 confirmed Bundibugyo Ebola cases (over 1,000 by June 24) across Ituri (817 cases, 91.1%, 21/36 health zones), North Kivu (~60+ cases, 11/35 health zones), and South Kivu (1/34 health zones), with no licensed Bundibugyo vaccine available. While Ituri remains the conflict-ridden epicenter with 4,659 contacts and ongoing expansion into new health zones, North Kivu is accelerating rapidly—jumping from 7 to 11 affected health zones and 699 to 1,628 contacts in 11 days, with Goma already impacted and high displacement—making Ituri and North Kivu near-even co-favorites for a mid-September weekly surge. South Kivu (already affected and linked to Goma across Lake Kivu) is the main tertiary risk, with adjacent provinces Tshopo and Haut-Uele holding smaller spillover probabilities.

The three affected provinces in eastern DRC — Ituri, North Kivu, and South Kivu — have been plagued for three decades by conflict and mass displacement, complicating the response. The outbreak has spread to Uganda, where containment measures have been effective. Kampala has reported 20 confirmed cases nationwide, including two deaths, since May 15. Most of those infected are Congolese nationals who have traveled to Uganda. questions.title: Which country will agree to a joint project with Iran to clear sea mines from the Strait of Hormuz by August 26, 2026?
questions.background: Sea mines have been reported near the Strait of Hormuz, a major route for international oil and gas shipments.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Resolve to the country that agrees with Iran to a joint mine-clearance project in the Strait of Hormuz, as announced in a statement from the two governments by August 26, 2026. Resolution Date : 2026-08-26 Accepted Answer Format : Answer with the country's common English name.
questions.current_reasoning: June 27 local reporting (Reuters via Irish Times/Straits Times, Al Jazeera, and Hindustan Times/Bloomberg) clarifies two important developments despite Saturday's US-Iran retaliatory strikes (including an alleged Iranian drone strike on Bahrain): (1) Even after Oman signed the US-GCC statement and Friday's CENTCOM strikes, Iran's Foreign Ministry explicitly affirmed that 'the strait should be governed by Iran and Oman,' while Bloomberg reports Oman told European officials shipping fees for navigation/de-pollution services may be necessary—echoing the June 23 Iran-Oman bilateral working group—and Sultan Haitham meets Macron in Paris on Monday June 29, while the IMO estimates ~80 mines remain in the shared Traffic Separation Scheme; this reverses yesterday's dip on Oman, lifting Oman from 0.28 to 0.32. (2) Hindustan Times also highlights that Pakistan—broker of the Islamabad MoU (with its 30-day mine-clearing clause) and operator of nearby naval minehunters—is already coordinating navigational warnings and reported detecting a mine near Oman, lifting Pakistan from 0.12 to 0.14 ahead of Russia (0.12), while trimming China slightly (0.24 to 0.22) and US ally Japan (0.06 to 0.05) amid active US-Iran fire, leaving 15% tail mass.

questions.title: Which international organization, if any, will first gain direct access to Aung San Suu Kyi in detention during 2026?
questions.background: Aung San Suu Kyi has been detained since Myanmar's military overthrew her government in February 2021. Her access to outside visitors has been tightly restricted.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Public statements from the visiting organization or Myanmar authorities, corroborated by established news reporting. Qualifying Event : Direct access means a completed in-person meeting with Suu Kyi by a representative acting on behalf of an international organization. Permission or an announced plan without a completed visit does not qualify. Resolution : Resolve to the first international organization publicly confirmed to have completed such a visit during 2026. If no qualifying visit is confirmed by December 31, 2026, resolve that no organization qualified. Accepted Answer Format : The organization's name, or a statement that no organization qualified.
questions.current_reasoning: No international organization has gained direct access to Aung San Suu Kyi in over five years since February 2021, anchoring a substantial 35% baseline for no organization qualifying in 2026. However, Min Aung Hlaing's April 2026 inauguration as president and the regime's April 30 transfer of Suu Kyi to house arrest ahead of the Cebu ASEAN Summit create a real opening for a controlled visit. The ICRC is best positioned for a confidential medical/proof-of-life visit (explicitly urged by Kim Aris in April 2026), while 2026 ASEAN Chair the Philippines and ASEAN Special Envoy Ma. Theresa Lazaro formally demanded a meeting with Suu Kyi in May 2026; the UN faces steeper regime distrust.

local_articles.title: Son of Myanmar’s Aung San Suu Kyi demands proof of life from military government
local_articles.snippet: The younger son of Myanmar’s imprisoned pro-democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi is calling for the country’s military-led government to provide proof that she is alive, after it claimed in April that her sentence was commuted to around 17 years and that she had been moved to house arrest. questions.title: Who will be appointed to succeed Pape Thiaw as head coach of Senegal's men's national football team by August 31, 2026?
questions.background: The Senegalese Football Federation is responsible for appointing the national team's head coach.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : An official announcement by the Senegalese Football Federation, as confirmed by contemporaneous reliable news reporting. Resolution : Resolve to the person publicly announced as Pape Thiaw's successor between August 1 and August 31, 2026. The resolution date is the date the appointment is publicly announced, rather than the coach's presentation or first match. Accepted Answer Format : The appointed coach's full name.
questions.current_reasoning: Despite signing a belated contract extension on June 21 after months of friction with the FSF and a five-match CAF ban from the controversial Jan 2026 AFCON final, Pape Thiaw is under severe pressure with Senegal 0–2 at World Cup 2026 (losses to France and Norway). Conditioning on an August 2026 replacement announcement with no shortlist yet formed, the FSF has strongly favored former Senegalese internationals and internal youth-title winners (Habib Beye, Omar Daf, Malick Daf) or proven Francophone African specialists (Hervé Renard), alongside a possible return for former champion Aliou Cissé. Given high pre-vacancy candidate entropy across 15+ plausible Senegalese and French coaches, these top five sum conservatively to 43%.

questions.title: Which candidate will receive the most “encourage” votes in the first UN Security Council straw poll of the 2026 secretary-general selection?
questions.background: António Guterres is serving as UN secretary-general. Informal Security Council straw polls gauge support for potential successors, with members indicating whether they encourage, discourage or have no opinion on each candidate.
questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official UN information or contemporaneous reporting by reputable international news organizations describing the first Security Council straw poll in the 2026 secretary-general selection process. Resolution Condition : Resolve to the candidate receiving the highest number of “encourage” votes in that first poll, regardless of subsequent polls or the final appointment. Accepted Answer Format : The candidate’s full name.
questions.current_reasoning: As of mid-June 2026, only four active nominees remain for the late-July UN Security Council straw polls: Rebeca Grynspan, Rafael Grossi, Michelle Bachelet, and Macky Sall (Virginia Gamba withdrew in March). Grynspan (UNCTAD head, Costa Rica) holds the edge for most 'encourage' votes in the undifferentiated first poll because she satisfies both the historic push for a first female UNSG and GRULAC rotation while enjoying strong Global South, European, and pragmatic P5 acceptability. Grossi (IAEA chief, Argentina) is a formidable second with high diplomatic stature and strong US/Western backing (mirroring Guterres's 2016 agency-head lead), while Bachelet is severely handicapped by Chile's March 24 withdrawal of support and US opposition, Sall lacks AU endorsement, and Mia Mottley represents the main late-entrant tail.
